summary: New nether biomes don t work properly in buffet worlds
description: The bug The new nether biomes (nether wastes, soul sand valley, crimson forest, warped forest and basalt deltas) do not work in Surface or Floating Island Buffet worlds. To reproduce - Create New World - Select More World Options - Make a buffet world - Select Soul Sand Valley - Set terrain type to Floating Islands or Surface Floating Island mode Freezes the game before it even loads terrain (Image Below) -Surface mode creates a purely ocean world (This happened the first time i tried to make one but works fine now for some reason) The following list is updated in version 20w15a: Biomes All world generators that freeze the game Nether wastes Surface Crimson forest Surface Warped forest Surface and floating islands Soul sand valley Surface Basalt deltas Surface
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Launch Minecraft and select **Singleplayer → Create New World**.  
2. Open **More World Options**.  
3. Enable the **Buffet world** setting.  
4. Choose a nether biome (e.g., **Soul Sand Valley**) from the biome list.  
5. Set **Terrain Type** to **Floating Islands** (or **Surface**).  
6. Confirm the settings and create the world.  
7. Wait at least a few minutes while the world loads.  
8. Observe that the game freezes or stalls before any terrain appears (or, for Surface, only an ocean surface is generated).
Observed Behavior: When a player creates a new world, enables the “More World Options” menu, selects the buffet world type and then chooses any of the new Nether biomes – Nether Wastes, Soul Sand Valley, Crimson Forest, Warped Forest or Basalt Deltas – the game does not generate the expected terrain and instead becomes unresponsive or loads for an excessively long time. In the Surface terrain setting the world may sometimes finish loading but often produces a world that consists only of ocean blocks, as was observed on the first attempt to create such a world, while on later attempts the same setting can appear to work correctly for some users. The Floating Islands setting is far more problematic: selecting Soul Sand Valley, Crimson Forest, Warped Forest or Basalt Deltas on a floating‑island buffet world causes the loading screen to stall at roughly two percent and remain stuck for hours, with only the central chunks ever appearing. Logs from the frozen sessions contain a warning line stating “Unable to find spawn biome”, indicating that the generator cannot place a valid spawn point for the chosen biome. Users have reported that the freeze is not a true deadlock – the game continues to run but the terrain generation proceeds at an unnaturally slow pace, sometimes taking four hours to finish the central area before the player must terminate the process via the task manager. The issue persists across several snapshots, starting with 20w07a where the load stalls at one to two percent, continuing through 20w10a where Surface and Cave generation work but Floating Islands still fail, and remaining present in 20w14a where Warped Forest on floating islands also hangs at two percent. Additional comments note that the problem is not limited to a single biome; Warped Forest, Crimson Forest and the generation of basalt pillars are also affected, and the bug appears to be unrelated to iron door functionality. Although some users have reported that Surface generation works for them, the overall behavior is inconsistent, and the bug was marked as fixed for all Nether biomes in a later update but later comments suggest the fix was either incomplete or reverted, leaving the issue unresolved in current versions.
Expected Behavior: When a player creates a new buffet world, chooses a Nether biome such as Soul Sand Valley, and selects Surface or Floating Islands terrain, the game should start generating the world normally, load the terrain within a reasonable time, and produce a surface that reflects the selected Nether biome (e.g., soul sand, basalt pillars, appropriate vegetation) without freezing or defaulting to an ocean‑only landscape.
